strings.d1.s0.name: Aya Yorgi Church
strings.d1.s0.tips: Take the 09:00 ferry from Kabataş; from the pier, ride an electric minibus or walk 40 minutes uphill to Yücetepe. The hilltop church has views over the Marmara.
strings.d1.s1.name: Yücetepe Kır Gazinosu
strings.d1.s1.tips: Köfte (grilled meatballs) and gözleme (stuffed flatbread) with a view, just below Aya Yorgi.
strings.d1.s2.name: Nakibey Beach, Büyükada
strings.d1.s2.tips: A family beach on the south of the island; service boat and sun lounger included.
strings.d1.s3.name: Luna Park Square, Büyükada
strings.d1.s3.tips: The pine-shaded square in the middle of the island; the starting point for bike tours.
strings.d1.s4.name: Ali Baba Restaurant Büyükada
strings.d1.s4.tips: A long-established fish restaurant beside the pier; meze and fish, with a heated enclosed section in winter.
strings.d1.b0.name: Milto Restaurant Büyükada
strings.d1.b1.name: Eskibağ Beach, Büyükada
strings.d1.b1.tips: A pine-shaded beach on the west of the island; an alternative to Nakibey.
strings.d2.s0.name: Büyükada Bike Rental
strings.d2.s0.tips: Bike rental behind the pier (about 300 TL/day); the full island loop is 12 km.
strings.d2.s1.name: Büyükada Grand Tour Road
strings.d2.s1.tips: A paved road around the island, with pine forest and coves.
strings.d2.s2.name: Dil Burnu
strings.d2.s2.tips: A nature park at the island's southern tip; swimming and picnics in summer.
strings.d2.s3.name: Büyükada Kalpazankaya Restaurant
strings.d2.s3.tips: Seaside fish and meze at Kalpazankaya; famous for its sunsets.
strings.d2.s4.name: Çankaya Avenue Mansions, Büyükada
strings.d2.s4.tips: Greek mansions and John Pasha Mansion; wooden architecture.
strings.d2.b0.name: Kalpazankaya Beach, Büyükada
strings.d2.b0.tips: A rocky beach; an alternative to Dil Burnu.
strings.d2.b1.name: Lokmacı Square, Büyükada
strings.d2.b1.tips: Hot lokma (syrupy doughnut bites) on the square.
strings.d3.s0.name: Heybeliada Halki Seminary
strings.d3.s0.tips: A Greek Orthodox school from 1844 on the hilltop; gardens and views, visits are guided.
strings.d3.s1.name: Çam Limanı, Heybeliada
strings.d3.s1.tips: A cove in the pine forest; swimming and picnics in summer.
strings.d3.s2.name: Heybeliada Square Fish Restaurant
strings.d3.s3.name: Heybeliada Naval High School Shore
strings.d3.s3.tips: A coastal road and the Aya Triada monastery; ferry back.
strings.d3.b0.name: Heybeliada Lokantası
strings.d3.b1.name: Değirmen Tepesi, Heybeliada
strings.d4.s0.name: Sait Faik Museum, Burgazada
strings.d4.s0.tips: The writer's house; the literary heart of the island.
strings.d4.s1.name: Kalpazankaya, Burgazada
strings.d4.s1.tips: Burgaz's western cove; swimming in summer, famous for its sunsets.
strings.d4.s2.name: Burgazada Kalpazankaya Restaurant
strings.d4.s2.tips: Fish and meze in the cove.
strings.d4.s3.name: Kınalıada Beach
strings.d4.s3.tips: The smallest island; red earth and a seaside walk, with a ferry transfer.
strings.d4.b0.name: Burgazada Square Breakfast Place
strings.d4.b1.name: Aya Yani Church, Burgazada
strings.d4.b1.tips: The church on the square; an alternative to the cove.
strings.d5.s0.name: Princes' Islands Museum
strings.d5.s0.tips: The history of the islands at Aya Nikola; Greek, Armenian and Jewish heritage.
strings.d5.s1.name: Hamidiye Mosque, Büyükada
strings.d5.s1.tips: Abdülhamid II's mosque, near the pier.
strings.d5.s2.name: Büyükada Greek Orphanage Viewpoint
strings.d5.s2.tips: Europe's largest wooden building, seen from outside; walk in the forest.
strings.d5.s3.name: Prinkipo Breakfast, Büyükada
strings.d5.s4.name: Yörükali Beach, Büyükada
strings.d5.s4.tips: A sandy beach; swim in the afternoon.
strings.d5.b0.name: Büyükada Ice Cream Shop, Square
strings.d5.b0.tips: Island ice cream; a light lunch.
strings.d5.b1.name: Aya Dimitri Church, Büyükada
strings.d5.b1.tips: A Greek church; an alternative to the mosque.
strings.d6.s0.name: Sedef Island
strings.d6.s0.tips: 10 minutes by boat from Büyükada; private island beach, sun lounger included, clear water.
strings.d6.s1.name: Sedef Island Beach Restaurant
strings.d6.s2.name: Aya Nikola Beach, Büyükada
strings.d6.s2.tips: The island's east shore; rocks, and a good spot before sunset.
strings.d6.b0.name: By Şükrü Restaurant Büyükada
strings.d6.b0.tips: A fish restaurant on Gülistan Avenue.
strings.d6.b1.name: Büyükada Public Beach
strings.d6.b1.tips: A free beach; an alternative to Sedef.
strings.d7.s0.name: Pier Square, Büyükada
strings.d7.s0.tips: The clock tower and square; quiet in the morning.
strings.d7.s1.name: Büyükada Pastry Shop, Square
strings.d7.s1.tips: An island pastry shop; breakfast and ice cream.
strings.d7.s2.name: Plane Tree Square, Büyükada
strings.d7.s2.tips: A last walk; the 12:30 ferry to Kabataş.
strings.d7.b0.name: Pier Tea Garden, Büyükada
strings.d7.b0.tips: Tea and simit (sesame bread ring) at the pier; a farewell.
strings.d7.b1.name: Gülistan Avenue, Büyükada
strings.d7.b1.tips: A street of fish restaurants; seafront.
strings.note0: Ferries run from Kabataş and Bostancı (Istanbulkart accepted): every 30 minutes in summer, hourly in winter; the last ferry leaves around 20:00.
strings.note1: There are no cars on the island: use an electric minibus, a bike or your feet. The Aya Yorgi climb takes 40 minutes; an electric vehicle costs 100 TL.
strings.note2: Summer weekend ferries are very crowded, so go on a weekday. Beaches cost 500 TL, sun lounger included.
strings.note3: Try hot lokma, island ice cream and fish with meze; the restaurants on Gülistan Avenue don't need reservations.
strings.note4: There are few ATMs on the island, so bring cash.
strings.note5: The ferry between the islands takes 15 minutes.
